prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · REST endpoints (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Endpoint" · longest unbreakable word 261px · one-line width 261px
  col 2: header "Method" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Auth" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "Rate limit" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 85px · one-line width 670px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1A: widths [282, 76, 67, 89, 205] · table 720×415px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [284, 76, 67, 89, 203] · table 720×415px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [300, 76, 67, 89, 187] · table 720×485px · row heights [36, 129, 129, 60, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [294, 76, 67, 89, 193] · table 720×461px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 60, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [308, 76, 67, 89, 179] · table 720×485px · row heights [36, 129, 129, 60, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [286, 76, 67, 89, 201] · table 720×438px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [284, 76, 67, 78, 214] · table 720×438px · row heights [60, 106, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [294, 76, 67, 78, 204] · table 720×438px · row heights [60, 106, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r1A","r1B"],"acceptable":["r3A","r3B","r3C","r2B"],"bad":[{"design":"r2A","why":"Endpoint has 18px of unused content width beyond the longest path while Description is squeezed to 187px, forcing five-line descriptions in three rows and a 485px table; the extra endpoint space is visibly idle."},{"design":"r2C","why":"This is the most over-allocated endpoint column (26px of unused content width) and the narrowest Description (179px), so descriptions run to five lines and the table grows to 485px for no identifier benefit."}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[282,284],[76,78],[67,69],[89,91],[203,205]],"rationale":"The endpoint paths are unbreakable row keys, so they must stay on one line; once Endpoint reaches about 282px, additional width there buys nothing and only steals from Description. Method, Auth and Rate limit are short categorical columns that should be just wide enough for their headers, with Rate limit at 89px or more so its two-word header stays on one line. Description should get the remaining width down to about 203px, which keeps the longest descriptions at four lines; r1A and r1B are effectively the same solution, differing only in whether the last 2px go to Endpoint or Description.","principles":{"general":["Allocate width by each column's role and minimum content, not by symmetry: hard-to-break identifiers need a firm minimum, short categorical columns need only header width, and prose gets the remainder.","Do not give slack to a column that already fits at the expense of the column that determines row height; small changes in the prose column can add a whole line and inflate the table.","A single-line header row is worth protecting, but a two-line header can be an acceptable tradeoff if it materially improves the main prose column."],"specific":["Endpoint needs roughly 282–284px (261px content plus padding) to keep every API path on one line.","Rate limit needs at least 89px to keep its header on one line; at 78px it wraps to 'Rate / limit'.","Description needs at least about 203px to keep the longest descriptions at four lines; at 201px the first row gains a fifth line.","r2A and r2C over-widen Endpoint to 300/308px while starving Description to 187/179px, producing five-line rows and a 485px table."]},"tradeoffs":"r3B/r3C trade a wrapped 'Rate limit' header for a wider Description; some designers would accept that because the prose line breaks improve, while others would keep the header row clean. r2B is a middle ground with a little endpoint breathing room and slightly taller rows.","uncertain":"Whether the extra prose width in r3B/r3C is worth the wrapped header, and whether 2px of endpoint slack in r1B is worth 2px less Description. The exact 203px Description threshold is renderer-dependent, so the boundary could shift by a pixel or two."}
